title: Chess, But Pieces Fall Through Breaking Squares
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where every square cracks each time a piece is placed on it; on the third placement the square breaks away and the piece standing on it falls through and is lost. Broken squares are permanent holes. The narrator pre-cracks his own half twice so attackers fall through, traps pieces on twice-cracked squares, and wins when the black king steps onto a twice-cracked square and falls (king lost = game lost).
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
Each time a piece lands on (is placed on) a square, that square gains one crack. Initial setup does not count [inferred].
When a piece is placed on a square that already has 2 cracks (third use), the square breaks: the piece falls and is removed, and the square becomes a permanent hole.
Castling cracks both the king's and rook's destination squares.
Holes are unplayable: pieces cannot move onto them (sliders presumably blocked through them [inferred]).
A capture onto a twice-cracked square loses the capturing piece too (both pieces gone).
A king that falls through is lost and that side loses the game.
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish or make its king fall through a breaking square (how the video ended).

board.shape_notes: standard 8x8; squares progressively crack and become holes
board.theme_notes: brown/cream board; crack line overlays (bigger with each use); broken squares are black holes with piece falling.

events: Crack counter increments on landing; break + fall on 3rd landing.
current_impl_issues: Legacy 'breaking': only middle squares crack, cracking when a piece LEAVES and breaking on the second time - wrong. Real: every square, cracks on placement, breaks on the 3rd placement, piece placed there falls (king loss ends game).
